title: Document that we are not working on --tls-details any more
body:
Document the parts that we have integration tests for, and make no promises otherwise.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
None
```

comments.body: Well this really sucks, should we remove this in a 7.0? I hated this from the beginning.

I don’t have much of an opinion.

Ideally, Go should follow the system crypto policies, and all of this should go away. I don’t think we can rely on that happening in any predictable timeframe.

If system policies aren’t an option, I think a feature constrained to registry accesses is still somewhat valuable — except that this does not cover _all_ registry accesses either (notably, IIRC builds), and even the parts that probably work don’t all have tests; so it requires very careful operation choice by users. Extending the support would, mostly, not be difficult work — the CLI integration with Buildah (where no support was merged) is probably the hardest part. It’s just a lot of code paths to test.

Alternatively, Skopeo does have the feature merged+tested, and in some situations that can be a sufficient workaround: instead of using a remote registry, do a manual copy using Skopeo between a remote registry and a local registry (local `dir:`??), and then use podman with that local copy. That’s probably easier to institute as a rule where users can be confident they don’t miss anything, OTOH implementing such a workflow would also be burdensome.
